record.paper_title: Four nucleon systems: a zoom to the open problems in nuclear interaction
record.original_question: What missing nuclear-interaction physics causes realistic interaction models, including INOY and AV18 plus Urbana IX, to underestimate neutron plus tritium elastic cross sections by more than 10% in the resonance region near center-of-mass energy about 3 MeV? This problem is not resolved by the same off-shell effects, explicit three-nucleon forces, or nonlocal two-nucleon forces that improve lower-energy behavior, so the cause must be sought in interaction components that affect the negative-parity resonance region.

evidence.quote: Nevertheless this system contains two, spin degenerated, narrow resonances at low energy (Ecm ≈ 3 MeV), while ability of nuclear interaction models to describe scattering cross sections in this resonance region was put in doubt [15, 16].

Nevertheless all realistic interaction models, including INOY, underestimate by more than 10% elastic cross sections in the resonance region. Off-shell effects as 3NF or nonlocality of the force, which improve low energy behavior, do not give sizeable effect.
On the other hand contribution of NN P-wave becomes almost as important as one of S-waves in negative parity states for n+3H resonance region.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the four-nucleon scattering problem of a neutron incident on a triton (³H) in the elastic channel. The ⁴H compound system possesses two narrow, nearly spin-degenerate negative-parity resonances at low energy, producing a peak in the n+³H elastic cross section at center-of-mass energy E_cm ≈ 3 MeV. Solve the four-body scattering problem (e.g., via Faddeev–Yakubovsky, AGS, or hyperspherical-harmonics methods) using a realistic nuclear Hamiltonian H = T + Σ V_{NN} + Σ V_{3N}, where V_{NN} is a realistic two-nucleon interaction (such as AV18, CD-Bonn, Nijmegen, or a nonlocal interaction with one-pion-exchange tail like INOY) and V_{3N} is a three-nucleon force (such as Urbana IX).

Empirically, every such realistic interaction yields an elastic n+³H cross section near the resonance peak (E_cm ≈ 3 MeV) that lies more than 10% below the measured value. The following partial remedies are known to be ineffective for resolving this deficit: (i) modifying off-shell behavior of V_{NN}; (ii) including standard three-nucleon forces of the Urbana/Tucson–Melbourne type; (iii) replacing local two-nucleon forces by phenomenologically nonlocal ones. Since the deficit lies in the negative-parity resonance region, where NN P-waves contribute on a par with S-waves, the missing physics must reside in components of the nuclear interaction that act in odd-parity (predominantly P-wave) NN channels.

Problem. Identify the component(s) of the nucleon–nucleon and/or many-nucleon interaction whose inclusion or modification—consistent with current constraints from 2N and 3N data—simultaneously reproduces the measured n+³H elastic cross section at the resonance peak near E_cm ≈ 3 MeV (within experimental uncertainty) and the positions and widths of the negative-parity ⁴H resonances, without spoiling the successful description of low-energy n+³H observables (e.g., the doublet and quartet scattering lengths) and of A=3 binding energies.
artifact.status_search_result: Reviews of four-nucleon scattering subsequent to the original observation (including a 2019 Frontiers in Physics review by Lazauskas and Carbonell) report that the ~10% underestimate of the n+³H elastic cross section near the resonance peak persists across most realistic NN+3N models, with the deficit traced to insufficient attraction in negative-parity (P-wave) channels. Some chiral interactions (e.g., I-N3LO with a 500 MeV cutoff and accompanying 3NF) can reproduce the peak, but this is parameterization-dependent and not a systematic resolution. The problem is still regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Description of Four- and Five-Nucleon Systems by Solving Faddeev-Yakubovsky Equations in Configuration Space
status_evidence.snippet: Most of these models fail to provide sufficient attraction for negative parity states (essentially P-waves)... other parameterizations... are not so successful, underpredicting the total cross-section.
status_evidence.claim: The n+3H cross-section underestimate near the resonance peak persists across most realistic interaction models.

status_evidence.title: Benchmark calculation of n-3H and p-3He scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Benchmark of three independent four-body methods for n-3H scattering with realistic NN interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Independent calculations confirm the discrepancy is a feature of the input interactions, not a numerical artifact.
